<edits>
No components were edited. All candidate harnesses—inv1, dom1, and agg1—are byte-for-byte identical to the base_harness. Each candidate's harness.diff file shows "(no change)".

The three rollouts produced different final answers despite identical harness code:
- base1: "AB, ABD, ABC" (7570 tokens)
- inv1: "A, AD, AC" (7892 tokens)
- dom1: "A, AD, ABC" (9833 tokens)
- agg1: "A, AD, ABC" (5509 tokens)

These output differences are pure model variance during a single LLM call under identical harness conditions, not harness-driven divergence.
</edits>

<experience>
NO_ENTRY
</experience>

The record shows no edits to any candidate harness. All three independent decisions (inv1.md, dom1.md, agg1.md) concluded KEEP_BASE, citing a single successful baseline execution with no failure pattern to diagnose. The adoption of agg1 occurred at k=1 without a selection session. Since no harness components changed and output variance reflects model sampling noise rather than harness design, there is no execution contrast to support a transferable lesson.
